description:
FOUND s495f (probing #2103's vivifying contexts; scratch/s495f/p-viv.pl, p-viv2.pl, p-viv4.pl), PRE-EXISTING (identical on 3d9b3712).  THE CAUSE IS THE raw-slot KIND-A EMISSION: every row below is RIGHT under `PCL_OPT=-raw-slot`.

    my $u; push @$u, 1, 2; print scalar(@$u);
      perl: 2        PCL: dies "Type of arg 1 to push must be array (not constant item)" -- an SBCL backtrace, exit 1
    (unshift @$u / splice @$u die the same way)

    use strict;
    my $x; my $e = $x->[0];  print ref($x);     perl ARRAY   PCL "" (undef)
    my $y; for (@$y) { }      print ref($y);     perl ARRAY   PCL ""
    my $z; my @k = keys %$z;  print ref($z);     perl HASH    PCL ""
    my $s; my @sl = @$s[0,1]; print ref($s);     perl ARRAY   PCL ""
    my $p; my $v = pop @$p;   print ref($p);     perl ARRAY   PCL ""
  (`my $b; $b = undef; push @$b, 1` and `push @{$h{list}}, ...` are RIGHT: only a never-assigned `my $x;` that the verdict makes a raw `:scalar` slot is affected.)

The emission is `(p-let (($u :scalar (p-undef))) (p-push (p-cast-@ $u) 1 2) …)`: a raw slot holds the VALUE, so the deref has no PLACE to vivify into -- p-cast-@ answers a constant and p-push refuses it.  `my $list; push @$list, $x` is an everyday idiom (accumulate into a lazily created array ref), so the first row is a LOUD failure of ordinary code.
WHERE: the raw-slot verdict (Pl/VarAnnotator.pm / Pl/Passes.pm `raw-slot`) must DECLINE a scalar that is dereferenced in a VIVIFYING context (push/unshift/splice/foreach/keys/values/each/pop/shift/slices/element reads and writes -- the #2103 DONE note lists the perl-probed set), or simply any scalar that is ever the operand of a deref (`p-cast-@`/`p-cast-%`/`p-cast-$`, `->[`, `->{`): a raw slot cannot be a reference TARGET.  Measure first how many raw slots the corpus has that are deref operands (corpus-diff after the decline) -- the speed cost should be nil because a vivified ref slot is a box anyway.
BAR: Pl/ emission change => gen bump, corpus-diff read per file, full sweep, guard rows (the table above, differential), inverse-verified.  Priority: HIGH among correctness fillers (a common idiom dies).


=== DONE (s497b) ===
VarAnnotator: a `deref_base` fact is recorded for a bare `$x` that is the operand of a cast (`@$x` `%$x` `$$x` `$#$x`, `->@*`), the root of a `->[` / `->{` access, a slice base, `"@$x"`, and (text-shaped) a deref inside a closure body, a regex/heredoc leaf or a parse-failure fallback; a scalar with ZERO write facts (_name_touched) and a deref_base gets the reason `deref-of-unwritten` = a BOX.  Written scalars keep their verdict (the s473b accessor trap).  Runtime found on the way: ref() of a box holding NIL answered ARRAY ((listp nil) -> consp); `$$u = 1` wrote into $u instead of vivifying a SCALAR ref; an rvalue element read / `$#$u` / exists / delete did not vivify a box; a RAW undef reached p-cast-@'s fallback and was ONE element.  Probe table scratch/s497b/m1-probes.pl: 40 rows + 4 breaking cases identical to perl except the no-strict scalar count (#2408).  corpus-diff (member 1 alone): 2 files (ref.t/postfixderef.t `eval { my $foo; %$foo }` rows -> :box); emission-ab lib+cpan 432 SAME.  Guard Pl/t/deref-vivify-01.t (57 rows, inverse-verified: 45 fail on 24422497).  ir-spec Â§2.2.
subject: BUG (pre-existing): a never-assigned `my $u;` under the raw-slot emission cannot be VIVIFIED through a deref -- `push @$u, 1` DIES ("Type of arg 1 to push must be array"), and rvalue element reads / foreach / keys / slices / pop leave $u undef where perl makes it a ref
